trusted_external_entities.name: External Caller
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Contract or EOA making calls to affected contracts. No authentication mechanism, arbitrary external input.

trusted_external_entities.name: Block Proposer
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Miner/validator proposing new blocks with timestamps. Subject to consensus rules but can manipulate timestamps within bounds. Authenticated via PoW/PoS but inputs must be validated.

trusted_external_entities.name: Malicious Miner
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Explicitly modeled as attacker attempting to game uncle rate for increased rewards. Must assume worst-case behavior.

trusted_external_entities.name: P2P Peer Node
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Network peer announcing and serving blob transactions or receipt data. No cryptographic attestation of data validity, peer can send malicious or malformed data. All data must be validated before processing.

trusted_external_entities.name: Calling Contract
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Smart contract or EOA invoking MODEXP precompile via CALL opcode. Can provide arbitrary input data, no authentication. Full input validation required.

trusted_external_entities.name: Requesting Peer
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Node requesting receipt data via eth/70 protocol. Request parameters untrusted, can request arbitrary block hashes or indices.

boundary_edges.security_assumption: Contract must handle all external calls with gas repricing in mind. Hardcoded gas assumptions are dangerous.
Block header data authenticated via consensus. Difficulty value validated as part of block validation.
Uncle references validated cryptographically via unclesHash. Proposer cannot fake uncle presence.
Timestamp bounded by protocol rules but proposer has some manipulation range. Must be validated within acceptable bounds.
EIP-100 formula neutralizes uncle rate gaming attack. Attacker manipulation factored into difficulty adjustment.
Transaction hash announcement requires no trust. Actual transaction data must be fetched and validated separately.
Peer receives blob requests. Response data must be validated against vhashes before acceptance.
All blob data received from peers must have hash correspondence validated before use or forwarding.
Input data is arbitrary and untrusted. Zero-padding semantics handle short input. Length fields must be parsed carefully to prevent overflow.
Partial receipt data from peers requires full validation before acceptance. Sanity checks on count, size bounds mandatory.
Complete receipt responses must still be validated. Receipt count must match transaction count, sizes must be bounded.
Request parameters untrusted. Block hashes must be validated as known. Index values must be bounds-checked. Rate limiting recommended.
